title: Tenant Fidelity Experiments and Guardrails PRD
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This PRD describes a product-level capability for tenant-level fidelity experimentation and automated guardrails. The goal is to let product engineering and platform teams run controlled experiments that vary model fidelity (quantization, sequence length caps, hybrid routing to cheaper variants) per-tenant or per-route, while ensuring safety, quality and SLO compliance.

Context and motivation:

- Customers run diverse workloads and often want to trade quality for cost on a per-tenant basis (e.g., low-cost embedding pipelines vs. high-fidelity chat).
- Existing controls are route- and model-centric; we need a tenant-first experimentation surface that integrates with rollouts, billing, and console observability.
- This feature enables: targeted cost reductions, capacity-safe rollouts of quantization and small-model fallbacks, and learning-driven fidelity presets for different usage patterns.

Goals (what success looks like):

1. Provide experiment API and console UI to define per-tenant fidelity experiments (profiles) with guardrails that enforce baseline SLOs.
2. Automatic detection and rollback when quality regressions or SLO breaches are observed.
3. Tight integration with Redwood Console for visibility: per-tenant cost delta, latency distribution, quality regression alerts, and trace links into eval harness.
4. Billing metadata to track experiment-influenced cost savings and revenue attribution.

Non-goals:

- We will not change model training or create new model variants. This feature operates at serving/variant-routing, quantization, and runtime config levels.
- Not a replacement for full manual tenant migrations — complex customers will still use Dedicated/Private capacity pathways.

High-level product requirements (functional):

FR-01: Experiment definition API
- Accepts: tenant_id(s), route selector, fidelity_profile (named), start/end timestamps, traffic allocation (percentage), metrics to monitor, rollback thresholds, owner and tags.
- Example: POST /v1/tenant-experiments

FR-02: Fidelity profiles
- Prebuilt profiles (e.g., high, balanced, cost-optimized) and custom profiles that can set: quantization level (int8, int4, awq), max_sequence_length, fallback_variant (e.g., gpt-small-embedding-v2), batching strategy hints, and cache TTL.

FR-03: Guardrail engine (slo-evaluator microservice)
- Continuously evaluates experiment windows against SLOs: p95_latency, error_rate, quality_score (see metrics).
- If thresholds are crossed, trigger automatic rollback and notify owner.

FR-04: Observability and dashboards
- Per-experiment dashboard in Redwood Console with: cost delta, token throughput, latency histograms, quality score trend, and sample outputs for manual review.
- Link to eval-harness prompt sets and historical baselines.

FR-05: Billing and attribution
- Tag tokens/embeddings associated with experiments so finance can compute cost savings and adjust invoices/credits.

FR-06: Safe rollout policies and canaries
- Support phased rollout: baseline -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, with canary hold windows and automated progression if metrics stable.

Non-functional requirements:

NFR-01: SLO adherence
- Experiments must not allow a tenant-level p95_latency regression > 30% over baseline or error_rate increase > 0.5 percentage points without rollback.
- Quality regressions: automated quality_score delta threshold default -3 points (configurable).

NFR-02: Isolation and performance
- Experiment routing must not degrade global tail latency by more than 5ms.

NFR-03: Data retention and privacy
- Experiment traces and samples kept 90 days by default; ability to exclude PII.

Acceptance criteria:

- Create an experiment via API and see it appear in Console within 30s.
- Canary progression halts and rolls back automatically when configured thresholds are breached in a 5-minute window.
- Cost attribution tags appear on billing exports and link to experiment IDs.
- UX: Console shows quality score time-series and example response diffs for at least 10 sample requests.

Metrics and signals to monitor (minimum):

- p50/p95/p99 latency per-tenant and route
- error_rate (HTTP 5xx + inference errors)
- quality_score: composite metric (see appendix) combining eval-harness BLEU-like metrics and production feedback (sanity checks, rerank delta)
- token consumption and token cost delta vs baseline
- audio/embedding similarity drift (for multimodal tenants)

Operational design and components:

- route-manager: attaches experiment labels to incoming requests and routes to fidelity-controlled variant.
- fidelity-advisor: stores profiles, validates constraints, computes expected cost delta.
- slo-evaluator: streaming evaluation engine consuming traces and metrics, emitting rollback events.
- experiment-control-plane: API + console + datastore for experiment records (owner, status, metrics summary).
- billing-tagger: attaches experiment metadata for downstream billing pipelines.

Example fidelity profile (YAML-like):

---
name: cost-optim-2025
quant: int4-awq
max_sequence_length: 1024
fallback_variant: mix-small-embed-v1
batching: auto
kv_cache_ttl: 300
quality_thresholds:
  quality_score_delta_min: -3
  p95_latency_max_delta_pct: 30
---

Rollout flow (detailed):

1) Owner creates experiment with profile and phases.
2) System schedules canary at 1% for default 10 minutes and starts collecting metrics.
3) If metrics within thresholds, progress to 10% for 30 minutes, then 50% for 60 minutes, then 100%.
4) If any guardrail triggers (slo-evaluator), experiment enters ROLLING_BACK state and shifting traffic back to baseline within 30s.
5) Owner receives notification, postmortem link, and preserved sample diff set for root cause analysis.

Console UX notes (needs design handoff):

- Experiment create wizard with: tenant selector, profile chooser, custom profile editor, phased rollout schedule, alerting config, and fiscal tagging.
- Dashboard panels: Live summary, metric trends, example diffs, billing estimator, and action buttons (pause, progress, rollback, snapshot).

Security and compliance considerations:

- Experiments that surface customer content to eval-harness must redaction-sanitize by default and honor tenant data retention settings.
- Role-based access: only tenant admins and platform SREs can create experiments that target >10% traffic without explicit approval.

Rollout plan and timeline:

- Alpha (internal): 2025-06 — limited to internal test tenants and Redwood employees (route-manager + console MVP).
- Beta (select customers): 2025-09 — invited customers with dedicated support; billing tags for cost reporting enabled.
- GA: 2025-12 — full public release, documented in pricing and packaging playbook (billing model for experiment-attributed savings).

Dependencies and integrations:

- Eval harness (applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness) for quality baselines.
- Billing exporter and data warehouse for cost attribution (finance pipelines).
- Auth/roles service for approval gating.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: False positive quality signal triggers unnecessary rollbacks.
  Mitigation: Combine production quality_score with sampled manual review and widen canary windows by default.
- Risk: Billing attribution complexity for nested experiments.
  Mitigation: Define experiment precedence and a deterministic tagging policy.

Ownership and runbooks:

- Product owner: Maya Chen (product)
- Tech lead: Arjun Patel (eng-platform)
- SRE owner: Priya Desai (eng-sre)
- On-call playbook: see runbooks/experiment-rollback-response in eng-platform.

Open questions (for review):

1. Should experiments be allowed to target multi-tenant shared models on Dedicated clusters by default, or require isolation? (security trade-offs)
2. What is the exact formula for quality_score that balances eval-harness metrics and production signals? Define weighting.
3. Pricing model: how do we surface customer-facing savings from experiments vs platform-level cost shifts? Finance input required.

Appendix: quality_score (proposal)

- quality_score = 0.6 * eval_harness_baseline_score_norm + 0.3 * rerank_delta_norm + 0.1 * manual_sanity_checks_pass_rate
- Normalization: each component scaled to 0-100. Default rollback threshold: -3 points vs baseline over the canary window.

Release notes (short form for GA):

- Introduces Tenant Fidelity Experiments: per-tenant fidelity profiles, guardrails, canary progression, and automatic rollback on SLO/quality breaches.
- Integrated billing tags for cost attribution and Redwood Console experiment dashboards.
